name: Claim Jumper at the Creek Bend

content.narrative_hook: A stranger has staked his claim right on your boundary line at the creek bend. His pick is already biting into earth you turned yesterday.

beats.text: You follow the creek to where your stake should be. Someone's driven another one — fresh wood, still green.
He looks up from his pan, squints at you through sweat-streaked dust. Doesn't move aside.
"This ground's open," he says. His hands rest on his pick like a man who means to swing it."
The creek runs between you both, cold and indifferent.

victory.text: He backs off when he sees you won't yield. You replant your stake with a curse.

defeat.text: You walk away bruised, your claim line shifted downstream by three paces.

content.narrative_hook: An old hand offers to share his sluice line — but only if you work the upstream end, where the colour is thinner and the labour heavier.

beats.text: He leans on his windlass handle, watching you pan. You've been at it an hour for nothing.
"I got colour here," he says, tipping his pan. A few flakes catch the light."
"You take upstream, I take downstream. We split even." His eyes don't blink.
Everyone knows the upstream end is a duffer — but it's better than nothing.

neutral.text: Whatever you decide, the old hand files your answer away for later.

options.label: Accept the partnership
options.description: Take the upstream end — thin colour is still colour.

options.label: Decline and keep your own ground
options.description: You didn't come here to work someone else's claim for scraps.

options.label: Propose a different split
options.description: Offer to take upstream only if the split favours you downstream.

content.narrative_hook: You collapse beside your claim stake, using the mullock pile as a windbreak. The earth still smells of turned soil and sweat.

beats.text: The mullock pile rises like a small hill behind you — waste rock from weeks of someone else's labour.
Your hands won't stop trembling. Even asleep, your fingers twitch like they're still panning.
The wind dies down. Somewhere nearby, another digger's pick echoes against stone — a rhythm that never stops.
You sleep fitfully, dreaming of gold that turns to mullock every time you reach for it.

neutral.text: Morning comes grey and cold. Your body aches but the claim is still yours.

content.narrative_hook: The ridge trail connects the diggings to the township — a narrow track worn by thousands of boots carrying picks and hope.

beats.text: The trail winds along the cliff edge. Below you, a hundred claims stretch across the valley like open wounds.
Every few paces, a stake marks someone's boundary — fresh wood or rotting, depending on how long they've lasted.
A windlass creaks somewhere below. The sound carries across the diggings like a heartbeat.

neutral.text: You reach the township edge, your boots heavy with red earth.

name: The Cost of Colour

content.narrative_hook: Weeks of digging have worn you down to something harder and thinner. The colour you've found barely covers your camp trader's tab.

beats.text: You count your flakes on a tin plate — three days' work, maybe enough for flour and tobacco.
The old hands don't talk about how much they've found. They just keep digging, deeper every day.
Something shifts in the diggings — claims consolidate, strangers arrive with capital and muscle.

neutral.text: The fever builds. Tomorrow you'll dig deeper.

narrativeSummary: The diggings reveal their true cost — fortune demands more than labor.
